704828.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hwéks, from Proto-Indo-European *swéḱs. Cognates include Sanskrit षष् (ṣaṣ), Old Armenian վեց (vecʻ), Latin sex, and Old English six (English six).

704826.t: From earlier ἐνῴδιον (enōídion), from ἐν (en) + οὖς (oûs, “ear”) + -ίδιον (-ídion). The form was later altered to re-align with ὦτα (ôtă), the plural of οὖς (oûs).

704804.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *entós, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁éntos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁én. Cognate with Latin intus.

704869.t: Based on φ/π variation with the likely-related ἄφνω (áphnō, “suddenly”), Beekes and Furnee assume Pre-Greek origin, noting that the correspondence of -ιφ-/-πι- suggests that the original Pre-Greek term was pronounced with a *pʸ.

704838.t: From ἐξ- (ex-, “ex-, out-”) + αἱρέω (hairéō, “to take, seize”).

704818.t: The neuter inflected form of ἐνύπνιος (enúpnios).

704812.t: From ἐν- (en-, “in”) + τυγχάνω (tunkhánō, “to happen (to), I succeed, I light upon, I obtain”).

704816.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *h₁én Ancient Greek ἐν (en) Ancient Greek ἐν- (en-) Proto-Indo-European *swep-der. Proto-Indo-European *supnós Proto-Hellenic *húpnos Ancient Greek ὕπνος (húpnos) Proto-Indo-European *-yósder.

704848.t: From ἑξακοσιοστός (hexăkosĭostós, “six hundred”) + -στός (-stós), a variant of -τός (-tós, ordinal suffix).
